target.title: Apply Claw plugin artifacts
target.body:
## Summary

This is PR5 in the Claws OpenClaw stack, stacked on #101973 and aligned with RFC PR openclaw/rfcs#27. It turns confirmed `claws apply --yes` and `claws feed apply --yes` into a real plugin-artifact install path while keeping the first mutating slice intentionally narrow.

What this PR does:

- delegates Claw `plugin` artifacts through the existing plugin installer with `pluginOnly: true`, so Claws do not accidentally install hook packs through plugin entries
- applies workspace validation before plugin installation, records scoped plugin provenance for successfully installed artifacts before workspace writes, and records full artifact provenance after workspace apply succeeds
- keeps required non-plugin artifact surfaces fail-closed until their installers exist; optional unsupported artifact surfaces are skipped
- treats Claw artifact refs as warning/provenance metadata, not uninstall locks or ref-count ownership locks
- makes `plugins uninstall` warn when installed plugin records are referenced by Claws, then proceeds with normal confirmed/forced uninstall behavior
- keeps `plugins uninstall --dry-run` read-only by avoiding the Claw provenance lookup in preview mode
- canonicalizes artifact matching across exact npm versions, floating npm selectors, npm-pack, ClawHub selectors, local paths/file URLs, and local git selectors resolved relative to the Claw manifest
- respects effective plugin enablement/global plugin policy when deciding whether an installed plugin satisfies a Claw entry

## Stack

- RFC: openclaw/rfcs#27
- PR2 consolidated validation: #101328
- PR3 mutating artifact provenance refs: #101755
- PR4 workspace file apply: #101973
- This PR: plugin artifact installers plus warning-only uninstall provenance

## Behavior Notes

This PR deliberately does not add Claw-level `remove`, updater/status flows, rollback, automation installers, skill/MCP/connectors installers, or ClawHub discovery. Those remain later stack items.

Plugin uninstall behavior is intentionally not reference-counted: if a user uninstalls a plugin that a Claw references, OpenClaw warns that the Claw may break until the plugin is reinstalled or the Claw is updated, then honors the user's uninstall choice.

## Real Behavior Proof

Current-head lifecycle coverage includes a real local plugin Claw fixture. The E2E invokes the real CLI with `node --import tsx src/entry.ts`, applies a local plugin plus workspace files under `--yes --workspace`, and verifies plugin install records plus Claw artifact/workspace provenance.

## Validation

Run on WSL worktree `/root/src/openclaw-claws-pr5-installers` at head `e176653a517e101ffcb0f5cb30114b45ea48f79a`:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/claws/schema.test.ts src/claws/provenance.test.ts src/claws/artifact-installers.test.ts src/claws/workspace.test.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.test.ts src/cli/claws-cli.test.ts src/cli/plugins-cli.uninstall.test.ts src/claws/lifecycle.e2e.test.ts src/cli/program/command-registry.test.ts src/cli/program/root-command-descriptions.test.ts
```

Result: passed 3 Vitest shards: unit 79 tests, CLI 38 tests, lifecycle E2E 4 tests.

```text
git diff --check
node scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.mjs
```

Result: passed.

```text
pnpm exec tsgo --noEmit --pretty false
```

Result: still blocked only by existing unrelated baseline:

```text
src/secrets/config-io.ts(12,17): error TS4058: Return type of exported function has or is using name 'configWritePostCommitRollback' from external module "/root/src/openclaw-claws-pr5-installers/src/config/io" but cannot be named.
```

```text
codex review -c model=gpt-5.5 --base origin/user/giodl/claws-pr4-artifact-plan
```

Result: no high-confidence actionable correctness issues found after fixes for prior review findings.
